headline: Archives, scorecards and the forms that keep memory moving.

items.title: A gallery of memories: How Kolkata’s citizens are preserving the city’s Chinese heritage
items.summary: Inside Kolkata’s new Cheenapara Heritage Gallery, a 1960s restaurant menu, a Chinese-language newspaper and tooth-setter’s tools preserve the city’s Chinese history. Sayari Debnath also traces the community’s contraction after 1962 and the institutions it still maintains.
items.angle: The most revealing objects are ordinary records of work, food and association. Together they show preservation as more than saving buildings: it means keeping community spaces active, documenting who used them and refusing a city’s habit of treating residents as outsiders.

items.title: The Pittsburgh Parallel Parking Championship Edition
items.source: Why is this interesting? · Mark Slavonia
items.summary: A family argument over the best parallel parker became a six-year-old Pittsburgh street championship. Mark Slavonia reports on its one-run format, volunteer stations and wonderfully blunt scoring system: parking time multiplied by distance from the curb.
items.angle: The delight comes from operational care, not spectacle. No preregistration, ten minutes from arrival to scorecard, simple public rules and friendly marshals turn an everyday competence into a ritual people want to perform together.

items.title: Everything, Everywhere, All At Once
items.source: Jay Zuerndorfer & Ori · Tiny Awards 2026 finalist
items.dateLabel: 2026 · Archival pick · Interactive memorial · Free browser experience
items.summary: Jay Zuerndorfer turns the days after losing Ori into a scroll through call logs, photographs and fragments of routine. The page moves from day zero to day twenty, ending after the layers of early grief have been worked through.
items.angle: A quiet example of interaction serving emotion. The scrolling asks for patience, while dated fragments resist the urge to make grief neat. It shows how a webpage can hold private memory without turning it into disposable content.

items.title: Pomp and Circumstance
items.dateLabel: 11 Oct 2026 · 11am–1pm IST · Free with RSVP, subject to availability
items.summary: Historian V. Sriram traces Carnatic musician Muthiah Bhagavatar across performance, scholarship and institution-building. Bhagavatar composed more than 400 songs, introduced around twenty ragas, led Trivandrum Music College and founded a Madurai gurukula in 1920.
items.angle: Go for a portrait of cultural work that refuses a single job title. The programme connects composition, Harikatha, teaching and research, showing how one person’s curiosity can move between private practice, public performance and durable institutions.
